question.value: Do the earliest-stage brown dwarf candidate Ser-emb 16 and its surroundings show spirals and streamers like those around young stars, and what do they imply about accretion and magnetic fields?

evidence.quote: We present the first observations of a large-scale spiral and a streamer towards a very young brown dwarf candidate in its early formation stages.
The observations were obtained in Cycle 8 (PID: 2021.1.00134.S) in September, 2022.
We observed Ser-emb 16 with ALMA in the HCO$^{+}$ (3-2) line at 267.567 GHz in Band 6.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Line window bandwidth 117.18 MHz, resolution 244.14 kHz (smoothed ~0.3-0.4 km/s); continuum baseband 1875 MHz with 976 kHz channels

evidence.quote: The bandwidth was set to 117.18 MHz, which provides a resolution of 244.14 kHz, or a smoothed resolution of $\sim$0.3-0.4 km s$^{-1}$ at 267.5 GHz.
We observed Ser-emb 16 with ALMA in the HCO$^{+}$ (3-2) line at 267.567 GHz in Band 6.
We also report the first detection in the ortho c-HCCCH 5(2, 3)-4(3, 2) transition line for Ser-emb 16.
Interestingly, no molecular outflow is seen in the CO (2-1) line image.
One baseband was used for continuum observations where the spectral resolution was set to 976 kHz and the total bandwidth was 1875 MHz.
The synthetic beam size of the observations is 0.47$^{\prime\prime}\times$0.38$^{\prime\prime}$ or about 221$\times$179 au at the distance to Serpens.
Our chosen configuration was a maximum recoverable scale of $\sim$4 arcsec, and an angular resolution of $\sim$0.4 arcsec.

sensitivity.value: 1-sigma rms ~0.15 mJy/beam continuum, ~10 mJy/beam HCO+, ~7 mJy/beam c-HCCCH

evidence.quote: The 1-$\sigma$ rms is $\sim$0.15 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for the continuum image, $\sim$10 mJy beam$^{-1}$ in the HCO$^{+}$ line and $\sim$7 mJy beam$^{-1}$ in the c-HCCCH line.

evidence.quote: We find a model with an initial misalignment angle of 30$^{\circ}$ best matches the observed structure in the moment 0 map

results_numeric.quantity: HCO+ abundance in spiral from models

findings_qualitative.value: No CO (2-1) outflow detected within 10 arcsec

evidence.quote: There is no CO detection at a $>$2-$\sigma$ level within 10$^{\prime\prime}$ of Ser-emb 16.

claims.hypothesis: Ser-emb 16 is a proto-brown dwarf with spiral and streamer accretion structures
claims.experiment: HCO+ (3-2) moment maps of ALMA Band 6 data
claims.result: Blue-shifted spiral (~2000 au) and red-shifted streamer (~2900 au) around the source
claims.finding: Large-scale asymmetric accretion exists around a candidate proto-brown dwarf

evidence.quote: These observations show, for the first time, the influence of external environment that results in asymmetric mass accretion via feeding filaments

claims.hypothesis: The streamer triggers warm carbon-chain chemistry
claims.experiment: c-HCCCH moment map compared with streamer
claims.result: Emission peaks near the source, nowhere else along the structures
claims.finding: Streamer impact may produce warm carbon-chain emission

evidence.quote: The impact of the streamer has produced emission in warm carbon-chain species close to the candidate proto-brown dwarf.

claims.hypothesis: The origin of the spiral can be explained by simulations
claims.experiment: Twisted pseudo-disk MHD model and core collision SPH model fed into MOLLIE
claims.result: Both reproduce the curved structure and clumps
claims.finding: Both are viable; they imply opposite magnetic field strengths

evidence.quote: Two contrasting scenarios, a pseudo-disk twisted by core rotation and the collision of dense cores, can both explain these structures.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Streamer as outflow rejected given no CO outflow detection; attributed to infall viewed from a different orientation

evidence.quote: However, there is no detection of a molecular outflow in the CO (2-1) line

limitations_admitted.value: Velocity resolution inadequate to constrain kinematics

evidence.quote: This makes it difficult to constrain the kinematics of these structures.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only one HCO+ line, so no independent kinematic test
Models are tuned by eye to fit and not unique
Mass estimates depend on assumed excitation and abundances
